citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., and Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. EMNLP 2016.
creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang (Stanford University)
description: SQuAD is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text (span) from the corresponding reading passage. Questions were posed by crowdworkers, and the dataset is designed to challenge machines on natural language understanding tasks requiring lexical, syntactic, and world-knowledge reasoning.
name: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset)
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question in the development and test sets has at least 3 answers total (1 original + at least 2 additional). In the training set, each question has 1 answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was assessed using inter-annotator agreement: the second answer to each question was treated as the human prediction, with the other answers as ground truth. Human performance on the test set was 77.0% exact match and 86.8% F1. Mismatch occurred mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements. Additionally, 2.6% of questions in the development and test sets were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of each paragraph. Questions had to be entered in a text field, and answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were shown a sample paragraph with examples of good and bad questions and answers. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words without copying word phrases from the paragraph; copy-paste functionality on the paragraph text was disabled. Workers were recommended to spend 4 minutes per paragraph. For additional answers, each crowdworker was shown only the questions and paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span that answered the question; if unanswerable, they submitted without marking an answer.
rai:dataBiases: Crowdworkers were restricted to those located in the United States or Canada, which may introduce geographic and linguistic bias. Workers were encouraged to use their own words (copy-paste disabled) to reduce lexical overlap bias between questions and passages. The dataset is sourced exclusively from English Wikipedia, limiting domain and topic diversity to Wikipedia's coverage. Answer types are skewed: 31.8% are common noun phrases, 32.6% are proper nouns, and only 19.8% are dates/numbers.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages: (1) Passage curation — top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles by PageRank were obtained, 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random, paragraphs were extracted (stripping images, figures, tables, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters), yielding 23,215 paragraphs; articles were partitioned into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. (2) Question-answer collection — crowdworkers on the Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend) were asked to write and answer up to 5 questions per paragraph, with answers highlighted as spans in the text. (3) Additional answers collection — at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets to assess human performance and robustness.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, from which 536 articles were sampled. Individual paragraphs were extracted from these articles, with images, figures, tables removed, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters discarded, resulting in 23,215 paragraphs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: Answers are constrained to be spans from the passage, which is more constrained than free-form answers. The dataset does not provide answer choices, requiring systems to select from all possible spans. 2.6% of questions in the development and test sets were marked unanswerable by at least one crowdworker. The constituency parse ceiling means 77.3% of correct answers are constituents, placing an effective ceiling on span-based methods. The dataset focuses on questions whose answers are entailed by the passage.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Wikipedia articles were filtered to the top 10,000 by PageRank; 536 were sampled uniformly at random. Paragraphs were extracted with images, figures, tables stripped out, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded. Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. For analysis, answers were automatically categorized using constituency parses, POS tags, and NER tags generated by Stanford CoreNLP.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive progress toward natural language understanding by machines. The authors note that the dataset presents a good challenge problem for future research, with human performance (86.8% F1) significantly above the best model (51.0% F1), indicating ample room for improvement in machine reading comprehension.
rai:dataUseCases: Reading comprehension and question answering research; training and evaluating machine learning models for natural language understanding; benchmarking progress on span-based question answering from passages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses, POS tags, and NER tags for automatic answer categorization and syntactic divergence analysis. Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks were used to rank and select source articles.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond noting that paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded (covered in preprocessing) and that some questions were marked unanswerable (covered in annotations).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper does not specify exact dates for data collection; only mentions 'over the last four months (since June 2016)' referring to model improvements after dataset release, not collection timeframe.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation or augmentation protocol is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described beyond the initial release (v1.0 is mentioned but no update cadence is stated).
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of Wikipedia passages and crowdsourced questions/answers; no personal or sensitive information is discussed.
null_reasons.license: The paper states the dataset is 'freely available' but does not specify a formal license.
